verdict.rationale: Perplexity ships an official MCP server, both remote-hosted at api.perplexity.ai/mcp and as a local stdio server, that exposes its search and reasoning as ready-made tools for AI assistants. It also offers a pplx CLI that returns JSON 'ready for shell pipelines and agent tool calls', so the core plug-in-as-a-tool part of the story is directly covered. However, the evidence shows no published function-calling schemas for other agents to consume. docs-62 describes custom function tools inside Perplexity's own Agent API, which is a different capability. There are also no named agent-framework integrations such as LangChain or LlamaIndex, so coverage is incomplete. missing for 10: published function-calling/tool schemas for direct consumption by external agents, documented agent-framework integrations (e.g., LangChain/LlamaIndex packages), independent or hands-on corroboration of MCP tool-call use.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can plug the API into an agent as a ready-made tool, with function-calling schemas and agent-framework integrations designed for direct tool-call consumption

citations.quote: The Perplexity MCP Server enables AI assistants to access Perplexity's powerful search and reasoning capabilities directly within their workflows.
Remote MCP server (recommended): hosted by Perplexity at `https://api.perplexity.ai/mcp`. No installation, nothing to update, works with any client that supports remote MCP servers.
Local MCP server: run the open-source server on your machine over stdio.
The Perplexity CLI returns the same ranked results as JSON, ready for shell pipelines and agent tool calls, with no code to write.
To restrict which tools the model can call, disable tools by default and enable the ones you want
